newsitem.title: UK: Politicians views on British budget.
newsitem.headline: Politicians views on British budget.

text.p: LONDON, July 2 - Following is a selection of quotes from leading politicians and members of parliament about the British budget, unveiled on Wednesday by finance minister Gordon Brown -
"When the Prime Minister (Tony Blair) said before the election, and I quote, "We've no plans to increase tax at all', he did not mean a word of it."
"This is a tax raising budget. When the Chancellor says he is tightening fiscal policy by 5-3/4 billion (pounds), he means he is introducing a tax raising budget."
"It is clear that this budget delivers a double whammy against pensions."
LABOUR MP RUTH KELLY, FORMER DEPUTY HEAD OF THE BANK OF ENGLAND'S INFLATION REPORT DIVISION.
"Gordon Brown's deficit reduction plan will create the conditions for businesses to flourish."

"Reducing mortgage interest tax relief and raising stamp duty on housing will remove anomalies of the tax system and ensure that the housing recovery does not develop into a fully-fledged housing boom."
"The budget recognises that economic efficiency and social justice go hand in hand."
